who: Night-shift hospital workers who sleep in daytime blocks
what_breaks: Wearable sleep scoring won't process a daytime sleep block on the day it happens, so the ring's core function is unusable on a night rotation.
quote: I can't even use my ring for its main purpose, to track my sleep. It used to be available the same day... my sleep doesn't update until almost 2 days later.
volume_evidence: 1-star review titled 'Oura Ring is awful for night shift workers'; Oura had 85 1-2★ reviews in the 2026-07-26 to 2026-09-10 window alone. Garmin's forums carry the same complaint across at least 6 separate multi-year threads.
workaround: Stops relying on the device; some shift workers manually re-enter sleep windows daily

who: Firefighters and others on 24-hour shifts who nap to repay sleep debt
what_breaks: Sleep-coaching apps won't count daytime catch-up naps toward sleep debt and won't ingest CPAP data, so the whole model is wrong for anyone not sleeping one night block.
quote: It also doesn't track when you take naps during the day to 'catch up on your sleep deficit' as I have to... not recommended for shift workers who take naps during the day.
volume_evidence: 2-star review on Rise Sleep; 60 1-2★ reviews sampled in a five-week window (2026-08-04 to 2026-09-11). Same nap-exclusion complaint recurs on Garmin forums across the fenix 7/8 and Forerunner lines.
workaround: Tracks apnea data separately on the CPAP vendor's own portal; ignores the app's sleep-debt number

who: Rotating-shift workers (nurses, plant operators, emergency services) using Garmin wearables
what_breaks: Sleep tracking classifies any sleep outside the configured bedtime as a 'nap', then double-counts it against the fixed window, so a night rotation reads as 16 hours of sleep or as zero.
quote: But being one of millions of shift workers I do find that all of the wellbeing apps and devices seem to ignore us. Come on, there is a wealth of free data here garmin.
volume_evidence: Garmin Connect forum thread open 11+ years and now locked, with replies still arriving years later from Vivofit 2, Venu, Forerunner 945 and fenix 6X Pro owners ('5 years Later. Unbelievable.'); three parallel threads exist on the fenix 7, fenix 8 and Forerunner 55 boards.
workaround: Setting the sleep window to 00:00-00:01, manually pressing the watch's sleep on/off buttons, or hand-editing sleep times daily in Connect — all of which break Body Battery and Training Readiness

who: Women who have had a miscarriage while tracking a pregnancy in a fertility app
what_breaks: Fertility apps have no state for pregnancy loss — a logged positive test can't be removed, dates can't be changed, and the app keeps surfacing the lost pregnancy.
quote: I miscarried, and it's impossible to change my pregnancy dates... once you log that test, it won't let you remove it. I'm so frustrated with this, and I pay for premium.
volume_evidence: 3 distinct Glow reviewers raise pregnancy-loss handling in the 92 1-2★ reviews I sampled (2025-01 to 2026-08), plus an independent Clue reviewer making the identical structural complaint — a cross-app gap, not one bug.
workaround: Some delete the app and start over elsewhere, losing years of cycle history; others keep two apps in parallel

who: Women trying to conceive who need to log a pregnancy loss without corrupting their cycle data
what_breaks: Cycle apps with a dedicated TTC mode still offer no way to record a pregnancy that ended, so logging it wrecks the cycle-length analytics the app is sold on.
quote: At least 10% of pregnancies end in miscarriage, yet there is no way to track a pregnancy on the app without messing up your cycle analytics completely.
volume_evidence: 2-star Clue review, from a sample of 90 1-2★ reviews spanning 2026-05-22 to 2026-09-10; reviewer notes support never replied and that 'they all seem to be just as terrible', matching the Glow cluster above.
workaround: Leaves the loss unlogged, or requests a refund and app-shops

who: People tapering off a prescription on a stepped-down schedule
what_breaks: Medication reminder apps can't represent a dose that decreases at fixed intervals — they scramble the strength and silently flip scheduled doses to 'as needed'.
quote: Trying to taper off an prescription at 14 day intervals is too much for this app to handle. It will mix up the strength of the dose and change the dates you set to 'as needed.' This is dangerous.
volume_evidence: 1-star Medisafe review; Medisafe produced 95 1-2★ reviews between 2025-06-24 and 2026-09-10. Taper communities independently distribute DIY spreadsheets (BenzoBuddies, Surviving Antidepressants) because no app does this.
workaround: "Going back to paper, pen, and calendar" — explicitly stated

who: Patients prescribed partial pills (one-and-a-half tablets, split doses)
what_breaks: Pill trackers have no concept of a fractional dose, so inventory and refill forecasting are wrong and every dose time has to be hand-corrected one medication at a time.
quote: I cannot properly track a medication because I take one and a half of that pill but for some reason a pill tracking app cannot rationalize that there's a concept of a half dose.
volume_evidence: Reviewer downgraded to 1 star specifically over this; sits inside 95 sampled 1-2★ Medisafe reviews. Half-tablet prescribing is routine across thyroid, cardiac and psychiatric meds, so the addressable population is large.
workaround: Manually editing each dose entry individually; abandoning refill tracking entirely

who: Adult children remotely supervising a parent with early dementia
what_breaks: The shared-caregiver view silently desyncs — the parent's med list shows on their phone but vanishes from the caregiver's, so the caregiver can't tell whether a dose was missed.
quote: The meds list suddenly disappeared from the 'friends' profile not allowing me to see if she take it or not... So it wont work for what I need.
volume_evidence: 4 separate Medisafe reviewers in my 95-review sample describe caregiver-view failures (dementia parent, post-surgery spouse, elderly mother); HN has an active Dec-2025 ask on exactly this coordination problem.
workaround: Phoning the parent to ask, or checking the physical pill organizer

who: Spouses managing a partner's post-surgical medication regimen
what_breaks: Medications disappear from the caregiver's linked profile while remaining on the patient's, and the only fix is deleting and re-adding each drug.
quote: multiple medications of hers stopped showing up on my app, but not hers, and did not even reappear after I tried refreshing... She had to remove these medications and re add them before I could see them again.
volume_evidence: Review titled 'Caregivers beware'; one of 4 caregiver-sync complaints in the Medisafe sample. The Dec-2025 Ask HN thread frames the same need: "the harder part seems to be certainty: 'Did I take it?' / 'Did you give it?'"
workaround: Switching back and forth between the two profiles to force a refresh; re-entering the drug list from scratch

who: People with a history of disordered eating who use a calorie app only for hydration or habit tracking
what_breaks: Streak/compliance notifications escalate into shaming language with no way to opt out of the weight-loss framing while keeping the logging tool.
quote: I struggled with eating problems a few years ago, losing a lot of weight in an unhealthy way. These notifications are strange and feel very very judgmental at times.
volume_evidence: MyFitnessPal generated 125 1-2★ reviews in just 25 days (2026-08-17 to 2026-09-11); multiple others in the same sample demand a way to disable gamification and streak pop-ups ('There are useless "streak" screens... Theres no way to turn these new gamification aspects off').
workaround: "Im just going to log my water manually with paper" — explicitly stated

who: Lifters training around an acute injury (wrist, shoulder, knee) who don't want to stop training
what_breaks: AI workout generators keep prescribing movements that load the injured joint and offer no substitution path, so the user stops training entirely.
quote: So many of these workouts require a body part that is currently injured and there aren't any options at times for alternatives... I'm at a loss losing muscle during this time.
volume_evidence: 2 distinct Fitbod reviewers raise injury limitations inside a 39-review 1-2★ sample covering only 2026-08-06 to 2026-09-10; a second reviewer signed up for a trial specifically because the vendor advertised an injury/limitations feature that wasn't in the build.
workaround: Manually swapping exercises before each session (which the app then reshuffles), or quitting the gym for the duration

who: Lifters running a fixed multi-week program who sometimes skip a set
what_breaks: Workout loggers can't carry a skipped set forward into the next session without destroying the rest of the edits to that workout template.
quote: There is no way to make skipped sets carry over to future workouts without losing other changes... People have been complaining about this for years on Reddit but it's still not fixed.
volume_evidence: Reviewer explicitly cites years of unresolved Reddit complaints; sits in a 45-review 1-2★ Strong sample spanning 2026-01-27 to 2026-09-04.
workaround: Re-entering the whole workout manually; a parallel reviewer of a competing logger calls it 'a glorified notebook' and says pen and paper is more effective

who: People with MCAS or other individualized food-reaction conditions
what_breaks: Meal planners only support a fixed list of named diets (vegan, keto, gluten-free) and offer no way to enter a personal list of trigger ingredients.
quote: I have MCAS so I have a highly restrictive diet. I understand not having low histamine as an option for diet, but there should be a way to manually add ingredients that I'm allergic to.
volume_evidence: 2-star Mealime review; the same 32-review 1-2★ sample (2025-07 to 2026-09) contains a Type 1 diabetic calling the app a 'Health Risk' because nutrition facts sit behind the paywall. Both are 'the diet model doesn't fit my body' complaints, not pricing complaints.
workaround: Keeping their own recipe list outside the app and cross-checking ingredients by hand

who: Manual-labor workers (construction, warehouse, trades) wearing activity trackers
what_breaks: The ring treats continuous on-the-job movement as dozens of unclassified 'active moments' and refuses to total daily calorie burn until each one is hand-confirmed and categorized.
quote: I work construction so naturally I'm moving around, a lot! ... I have to go back to the beginning of the day and start 'confirming' about 2 dozen 'active moments' throughout my day.
volume_evidence: 1-2★ Oura review from a sample of 85 covering 2026-07-26 to 2026-09-10; a second reviewer in the same window complains the ring logs daily activity as strength training and they're 'sick of manually deleting excerises'.
workaround: Manually confirming ~24 activity windows per day, or giving up on the calorie metric

who: Adult children managing an elderly parent's care across more than two hospital systems
what_breaks: Patient portals can only federate records when the hospitals cooperate and usernames match, so the family member ends up phoning offices to find out what an appointment change replaced.
quote: 'MyChart' Link My Accounts' is very difficult requiring more than 2 Hospitals to work together sharing medical data. Make sure you have the same sign-on name across all organizations.
volume_evidence: MyChart produced 36 1-2★ reviews in four days (2026-09-08 to 2026-09-11); a second reviewer in the same window describes spending '45 minutes trying to retrieve a message for my mother in law' and still having to call the office.
workaround: Maintaining separate logins per health system and phoning each office; some keep a personal spreadsheet of appointments and bills

who: Working adults with ADHD whose employer runs Outlook and whose tasks live in Todoist
what_breaks: Neurodivergent-marketed planners won't import an existing calendar or task system, so adopting one means rebuilding the user's whole external scaffolding by hand.
quote: You give an ADHD person an app that forces them to go back to their current system and change their calendar or change their to-do list that is actually torture.
volume_evidence: 2 separate Tiimo reviewers in a 48-review 1-2★ sample (2026-05-12 to 2026-09-10) name the missing Outlook integration; one title reads 'Not built for professionals — ADHD people need to hold jobs too man.'
workaround: Re-typing every recurring task into the new app, or abandoning it and going back to the raw calendar

who: Blind and low-vision VoiceOver users who need a modern note/document app
what_breaks: Premium note apps expose every control to the screen reader as an unlabeled text box and leave the document body entirely unreadable on Mac.
quote: All the controls are read aloud as text boxes, and the main documents are completely inaccessible on Mac... there was little to no consideration of visually impaired or blind users.
volume_evidence: 2 Craft reviewers and 1 Bear reviewer in my samples make the same structural complaint across competing apps (10 VoiceOver/blind-user complaints total across the 90-app corpus), pointing to a category-wide gap rather than one vendor's bug.
workaround: Deleting the app on day one and falling back to Apple Notes

who: Long-time task-manager users switching from iOS to Android
what_breaks: There is no task export, so migrating means reconstructing projects, recurrences and hierarchy from a partial database dump by hand.
quote: In the end I spent days getting a spreadsheet of my information and had to manually go through hundreds of records to update them.
volume_evidence: 2-star Things 3 review; the broader corpus contains 60 export/lock-in complaints across Evernote, Asana, Obsidian and Things, several from users with 4-13 years of accumulated data.
workaround: Building a spreadsheet from the exported database file and re-keying hundreds of records

who: Writers and worldbuilders using a markdown vault for long-form projects, not notes
what_breaks: After years, there is still no first-class export to a shareable document format, so images and links are effectively trapped and the whole investment becomes unusable off-platform.
quote: If I can't get my documents off obsidian aside from text files - what's the point of adding images? Whats the point of adding links? What's the point of using obsidian.
volume_evidence: 2 separate Obsidian reviewers in a 43-review 1-2★ sample (2026-01-16 to 2026-08-22) raise missing export/PDF on iOS; reviewer is a multi-year user describing projects, scripting and worldbuilding, not casual notes.
workaround: Exporting plain text and losing embedded media; hunting for community plugins that no longer load on mobile

who: Solo (non-team) users of team project tools who accumulated years of personal data
what_breaks: When a trial lapses, four years of personal task and calendar data is locked behind a paywall with no clarity about which paid features caused it, and the CSV escape hatch is unusable.
quote: My free trial ended today, and I was suddenly locked out of my main calendar with a message about custom fields, which I did not use... Exporting to CSV is not a solution.
volume_evidence: 1-star Asana review inside a 105-review 1-2★ sample spanning 2024-07 to 2026-09; part of the 60 export/lock-in complaints across the corpus, concentrated among users with 4+ years of history.
workaround: Wrestling with a 'disorganized mess' of a CSV; several users in the corpus re-key data into a spreadsheet

who: Quantified-self users trying to see labs, meds, glucose and wearable data on one screen
what_breaks: Health data is split across the provider portal, the wearable app and lab results with no tool that merges them, so the only unified view is a hand-maintained spreadsheet.
quote: So far I've been putting everything in an Excel sheet but I'm not a big fan of Excel and would like something standalone that might also show me progressions and changes more easily.
volume_evidence: 51-point Ask HN with ~30 substantive replies; a replier in the same thread writes 'I want to gather and have a single glass pane view of my meds, glucose, A1C, Weight, Exercise, Doctor Visits/Notes and Lab results', and another says they built a Google Form piping into Sheets in 2020 that is 'still going'.
workaround: Excel; Google Forms feeding Google Sheets; custom Grafana dashboards over an Apple Health export

who: Adult children remotely administering an aging parent's smart home from another state
what_breaks: Smart-home apps progressively restricted routine and device management to the local network, removing the remote-troubleshooting ability the setup existed for.
quote: I setup my mom's house (in Utah) with it and I regularly fixed her problems from Florida - but now it won't let me. Too many features only work now if I'm connected to the local network.
volume_evidence: 1-star review titled 'Worse Over Time — Update 2026 Aug — Still Degrading'; Google Home generated 107 1-2★ reviews in 18 days (2026-08-24 to 2026-09-11), a very high complaint rate for the category.
workaround: Talking the parent through fixes by phone, or flying/driving out to reset devices in person

who: Non-technical older adults forced to migrate off a dying password manager
what_breaks: There is no guided, verifiable migration path for someone who isn't fluent across iPhone and PC, so they are locked out of real-world services for weeks.
quote: It's been over a month since I have been able to do online banking. I have not deleted my LastPass account and I have to refer to it anytime I hope I can still log in somewhere.
volume_evidence: 1-star 1Password review; 22 1-2★ reviews sampled in a three-week window (2026-08-18 to 2026-09-09), several about vault migration friction. A Bitwarden reviewer in the same corpus: 'Not a good system for people that are not real savvy. I have to manually put in the username and password.'
workaround: Keeping the old manager alive in parallel and copying credentials over one at a time by hand

who: Drivers who switch between vehicles (rentals, work trucks, two-car households) using municipal parking apps
what_breaks: The license plate can't be corrected inside an active parking session, so a wrong plate means paying twice for the same space to avoid a citation.
quote: Could not correct license plate in active session. Customer service solution was to start another session and pay twice to avoid citation.
volume_evidence: 3 distinct ParkMobile reviewers describe paying twice over an uneditable plate or session within a single six-week window; 83 1-2★ reviews sampled 2026-07-28 to 2026-09-10, and reviewers repeatedly note there is no alternative payment method in their city.
workaround: Starting and paying for a second concurrent session; calling the parking office after the fact for a refund that usually doesn't come

who: Homeowners building a documented evidence log of a neighbor nuisance for a county complaint
what_breaks: Consumer security cameras trigger on motion, not sound, and enforce a cooldown between clips, so they cannot produce the continuous timestamped record a code-enforcement case needs.
quote: If it does record a bark, it gives itself a 5 min break before recording again. I need ALL the barks to be documented! Now I'm doing the work the camera was supposed to do.
volume_evidence: 1-star Wyze review from a sample of 94 1-2★ reviews in 25 days (2026-08-17 to 2026-09-11); reviewer bought hardware plus a paid plan specifically for this and discovered the limitation only afterward.
workaround: Sitting up at night and manually hitting record each time the noise occurs
